blocking.issue: Regression from the transport rewrite. The rule that admits Raft-class connections only 'from voter peer certificates' cannot be implemented as written, and it contradicts the owning document. No certificate records voter status: the owning document's certificate table issues one '8092 peer' certificate from the Peer CA, plus a 'relay' role certificate. Voter status therefore has to come from the Raft configuration, and a replica that is joining has none. After `Join`, the leader signs the replica's certificate, calls AddVoter and dials it with AppendEntries. A stream layer on the new replica that checks the literal rule has no configuration yet to find the leader in, so it refuses the connection and the join never completes. A replica restored from backup, or one bootstrapping the first configuration, meets the same chicken-and-egg problem. Replica roles item 4 of the owning document grants Raft 'for Raft members'. The release document's Ruralz Control upgrades rule 1 also names non-voter replicas, which are Raft members and receive AppendEntries. What the stream layer can check is the certificate role (Peer CA, role peer, never relay).
blocking.evidence: Transport row: "Only Raft-class connections from voter peer certificates reach `raft.NetworkTransport` via its `Accept`" / owning document, Replica roles 4: "Raft and write forwarding for Raft members" / owning document, Certificates and replica join: "| 8092 peer | Peer CA | 90 days (target) |" and "the leader signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter" / 04-release-versioning-and-compatibility.md, Ruralz Control upgrades 1: "Each replica, voter or non-voter, and each regional relay"
blocking.fix: Replace "from voter peer certificates" with "from peer-role certificates, never relay,". This adds two words, and the body is at 1,498 of 1,500 words. To stay in the band, also change "Node certificates are always rejected (TB-11)" to "Node certificates are rejected (TB-11)". Leave membership checks to raft itself, which ignores RPCs from unknown terms and servers.

non_blocking.suggestion: The edges `iface --> fsm` and `fsm --> raft` show the state machine feeding hashicorp/raft. In hashicorp/raft, writes go `raft.Apply`, then the log and quorum commit, then `FSM.Apply`, while reads come from the FSM. Draw `iface --> raft --> fsm`, with a separate read edge `iface --> fsm`, so the storage figure matches the Raft order that Figure 2 now shows correctly.

Say that leader services stop on leadership loss (the `LeaderCh` false edge), and that a proposal returning `ErrLeadershipLost` is treated as unknown: it may still commit, and it is neither re-signed nor reported as rejected. The rejection rule currently covers only an FSM rejection returned by `ApplyFuture.Response()`.

'only rejoining with an empty store reclaims space' overstates the cost. bbolt reuses freed pages, so the file stays at its high-water mark instead of growing without bound, and an offline copy with `bbolt.Compact` on a stopped replica also reclaims space. Consider 'bbolt reuses but never returns freed pages; reclaiming space needs an offline compaction or a rejoin'.

Every commit is slower across Regions because it waits for a quorum round trip, not because of the etcd election-timeout advice. That advice explains why timeouts, and so failover, grow. Reword to 'each commit waits for a cross-Region quorum round trip, and etcd advises election timeouts of ten or more round trips'.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (Transport row) and owning document
non_blocking.suggestion: A replica that redeems a token in `Join` has no client certificate. It must still authenticate 8092's server certificate, for example through a Peer CA fingerprint embedded in the one-time `admin` token, as Node tokens pin the 8091 server CA. The ADR and the owning document do not say this. Add it to the Proposed amendments for Control plane and GitOps, or to OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-15.

The owning document also says 'Replicas serve their Nodes from committed assignments' in Replica roles 1, and labels an edge 'committed assignments' in its Figure 1. Extend the reword request to both, as 'accepted assignments', so every place matches the fencing rule.
State that a backup pins the content referenced at its index while it copies, so a later Revision-deletion entry applied during the backup cannot remove an object the backup still needs.
